newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Support for main NZ coalition party falls - poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for main NZ coalition party falls - poll.

text.p: Popular support for the larger of two parties forming New Zealand's coalition government has fallen and the opposition Labour party has gained sharply, an opinion poll released by TV New Zealand said on Tuesday.
The monthly poll showed support for the centre-right National Party led by Prime Minster Jim Bolger had fallen six percentage points to 41 percent compared with the same poll a month ago.
Support for its partner, nationalist New Zealand First, was barely changed at 5.0 percent.
The survey was carried out among 1,000 voters for TV New Zealand's One Network News by pollsters Colmar Brunton in recent weeks.
Support for Labour advanced four percentage points to 36 percent and the five-party leftwing Alliance grouping inched up one to eight percent.
The free market ACT managed to increase its small share of the vote to six percent from four percent a month ago.
The poll has a margin of error of just over three percent.
